name: Devin Bruno
life: “I still remember a dog with a finer name than anyone on our street.” People around Tideline Market know Devin by a small Tuesday habit. Devin picks out the bruised fruit first and asks the seller what will ripen by supper.
voice: I don't know who loaned it to me. I remember their dog's name and hope somebody recognizes it.
appearance: Devin has a wide brow and a narrow jaw. Look for short black hair swept back. On an ordinary day, the familiar outfit is a pale blue work shirt with a pressed flower kept in the clear back of a phone case. In conversation Devin gives a little nod before asking a hard question.
personality: Devin never tires of being shown how somebody makes a living. Devin can ask an expert question of a craftsperson and still mishandle a simple emotional cue from a friend.
agenda: To identify the lender through the old dog's name.
family: Ivy Scott is Devin’s older relative by marriage. Devin can always ask for five minutes alone. Ivy asks before bringing somebody along. It keeps a conversation between two people from unexpectedly turning into a family committee. Asked about *The painted footprint*, Ivy says, “I came to see whether it was my foot before my toes began to curl.”
connections: Tali Allen. They look through remembered nicknames for the first owner of a borrowed mystery.

reactions.response: Devin lets the book go back with the note folded inside.

reactions.situation: The last bus leaves while an elderly stranger is still crossing toward it
reactions.response: Devin asks the stranger who will be expecting them, then helps find a way to tell that person.
